proposed_binary_target.negative_class: >=30 or NO (not readmitted within 30 days in dataset)
proposed_binary_target.clinical_definition_note: Positive class indicates an early unplanned readmission (<30 days). Negative class represents encounters with either late readmission (>30 days) or NO recorded readmission. Crucially, 'NO' signifies no recorded readmission within the 130 participating hospitals during the 1999-2008 study window, NOT medical proof that the patient was never hospitalized elsewhere.

verified_exclusion_codes.19: Expired at home. Medicaid only, hospice.
verified_exclusion_codes.20: Expired in a medical facility. Medicaid only, hospice.
verified_exclusion_codes.21: Expired, place unknown. Medicaid only, hospice.

hospice_86_breakdown.miscoded_status_evaluation: NOT MISCODED. All 86 encounters belong to disposition 13 (Hospice/home: 55 cases) or 14 (Hospice/facility: 31 cases). Exactly ZERO in-hospital deaths (codes 11, 19, 20, 21) have readmission labels (all 2,337 true in-hospital deaths have readmitted='NO'). Patients discharged to hospice are alive at discharge; these 86 cases represent genuine clinical palliative crises, hospice revocations, or symptom flare-ups leading to acute readmission. They are excluded under standard health-plan quality metric policies (e.g. CMS HRRP), which exclude all hospice discharges from readmission penalty benchmarks, not because of database error.

excluded_mortality_hospice.policy_rationale: Patients who expired in-hospital cannot be readmitted, introducing fatal survivorship bias. Patients transferred to hospice have fundamentally different palliative care goals and are excluded under CMS and health-plan readmission benchmark standards.

prediction_time_policy.rationale: The model is intended to run at the time of discharge planning to flag high-risk diabetic patients who require intensive outpatient care coordination, medication reconciliation, or post-discharge home health monitoring. At discharge, full inpatient duration (time_in_hospital), procedure counts, in-hospital lab tests, and medication changes are known.
prediction_time_policy.identifier_policy: Identifiers ('encounter_id', 'patient_nbr') are STRICTLY EXCLUDED from model features. They are retained solely for longitudinal linkage, patient-grouped cross-validation, and audit.
prediction_time_policy.discharge_disposition_sensitivity_plan: In Milestone 2, baseline modeling will execute an explicit sensitivity comparison: Model A (Clinical Baseline without discharge_disposition_id) versus Model B (Augmented Model with discharge_disposition_id). Even after excluding death/hospice codes, disposition codes (e.g. SNF vs home health) reflect post-acute placement decisions negotiated during stay, which could introduce circular placement leakage. The sensitivity comparison will quantify this impact.
prediction_time_policy.diagnosis_coding_sensitivity_plan: Similarly, final billed ICD-9 diagnoses (diag_1, diag_2, diag_3) are typically assigned post-discharge by professional medical coders. Milestone 2 will evaluate models with and without these discharge ICD-9 codes to assess lookahead coding bias.
prediction_time_policy.administrative_missing_features: weight (96.86% missing) and payer_code (39.56% missing) are dropped from clinical modeling due to non-random administrative missingness.

lab_distributions.clinical_category_note: The category 'None' in max_glu_serum (96,420 encounters) and A1Cresult (84,748 encounters) represents 'Test Not Performed/Measured'. It is a valid, clinically informative category, not a corrupted missing value.
